title: The staff client base — the same list twice
why: A legacy tab in `app.html` and the `AStaffClients` screen in `maya-os-site` are two implementations of one server projection: both read the same legacy proxy action `panel_master_clients` (L28522 / L25698) and both return a client list with revenue totals scoped to the logged-in master. Both already carry the `notmaster` state that explains an empty list to a non-master account (L28526 / L25702) — it is not a feature one of these two contributes to the other. The surface with no equivalent message is the SaaS clients tab they would fold into: the tenant-API-backed, manager-scoped `panel#clients` (L31305), which the evidence points at but which no signed record yet names as the target. Each copy survives only as a fall-through, and for different reasons: in `maya-os-site` managers are already routed to `panel#clients` (L23477), leaving `AStaffClients` as the implementation for non-managers; in `app.html` the staff bar prefers the SaaS cabinet and reaches the legacy tab only when the SaaS context is absent (L26474-26479). Collapsing them is ONE MAYA — DIFFERENT AUTHORITY: one `clients` capability whose scope — own clients or all — is decided by authority on the server, not by which of two screens an account happens to land on.
disappear: Both copies as separate surfaces — the legacy `app.html` tab and the `AStaffClients` screen in `maya-os-site/index.html` — together with the two primary-navigation entries they hold, two of the 101 Maya-owned primary-nav entries in the inventory (`NAV_BY_SCREEN_STAFF` `staff-clients`: 3, L39227; `STAFF_TABS` index 3, L25715). Neither disappears before parity: both rows are RETIRE AFTER PARITY — K16, and the successor on both is still `MERGE_TARGET — the surface it folds into, to be named` (successorSource: REQUIRES SIGNATURE). `panel#clients` is the evident candidate, but it is not itself a catalogued surface in this inventory — it has no disposition, no parity requirement and no risk note of its own — so naming it as the target is part of what the signature decides, not something the rows already establish.
remain: The master-scoped client list with revenue totals, as one `clients` capability with scope as a parameter rather than as a second screen. The `notmaster` refusal remains — but it has to be built into whichever surface absorbs these two, not inherited from it: the SaaS clients tab carries no equivalent message today. The staff bar indicator also has to be re-keyed, since the legacy tab's nav index is recorded as the only thing keeping that indicator honest on that screen.
risk: MEDIUM — merging the two copies into each other is cheap, since they are the same component twice, but that is not the edge that decides this. The target, `panel#clients`, is tenant-API backed and manager-scoped: merging into it without adding self-scoping would either expose the whole client base to a plain master or remove their client list entirely. Scope here is server-side authority over who may see whose client records, and since the fundamental rules hold fail-closed in only 13 of 21 cases, that self-scoping has to be demonstrated under the K16 parity condition rather than assumed to fail safe. Both copies also still run on the legacy `panel_master_clients` proxy while the target is tenant-API backed, so this is a re-implementation of the projection, not a re-parenting of it. It is not higher than MEDIUM because nothing is removed before parity: both rows retire only after parity (K16) and the successor is still unnamed pending signature, so the parity gate itself would have to fail before the exposure could reach a master's screen.
user_impact: Only a staff master notices anything, and barely. S-029 and S-094 are the same `AStaffClients` component, byte-identical, compiled into two separately-deployed bundles (app.html on malesthetic.pro L28513, maya-os-site/index.html on mayaos.ru L25689). Both call `panel_master_clients`, and both hardcode the SAME endpoint — `https://malesthetic.pro/app/api-proxy.php` — so they are not two lists for two populations but two front doors onto one backend and one salon's data; a master's session works in either bundle. (Drop the claim that "no single person ever had both": it is unevidenced and the shared hardcoded proxy makes it likely false. The load-bearing point is that both doors render the same bytes from the same call, so whichever survives looks identical and nothing visible is lost.) Correct also the dossier's own WHY line: the `notmaster` state is NOT added by the newer copy — the branch and the string `'Раздел доступен мастерам.'` are present identically in both. Today the master reaches this screen three ways, not one: staff tab index 3, the staff-home revenue tile (app.html:29178 / index.html:26358), and the staff swipe map (app.html:38973 / index.html:36016) — and the tab only lands here when `__ME_SAAS_CTX` is absent or the account is not a business role, since otherwise index 3 goes to `__meSaasCabinet('customers'|'profile')` (app.html:26471-26479, index.html:23472-23481). What it shows: visits this month, unique clients, new/returned, average check, "Заработал сегодня" vs "Потенциал MAYA", pace vs last month, an expandable name-plus-visit-count list with no phones, and the MAYA advice block. After, the same numbers arrive as one `clients` capability rather than a fixed tab. Two visible changes, not one: (a) a staff account the server says is not a master trades a dead tab reading "Раздел доступен мастерам." for no tab and a capability refusal; (b) in the mayaos.ru bundle the far more common dead state for any account that is not a malesthetic master is the generic `err` branch — "Не удалось загрузить. Попробуйте позже." — because the screen calls the single-tenant malesthetic proxy from the multi-tenant bundle. Parity note for the successor: the response payload already carries `gross`, `personal` and `percent` (the master's salary share) that this UI deliberately never renders; a merged capability must not start showing them.
security_impact: Direction is right and survives: neutral between these two rows. Scope is decided entirely server-side and the client's `notmaster` is only a rendering of the server's 403, so collapsing two identical renderers removes no load-bearing client-side check. Fix the citation: the gate is `webhook_server.py:3251-3282` (`panel_master_clients_handler` — `_panel_auth`, then `_panel_resolve_role`, `is_master`, `staff_id` from the resolved role, 403 `not_master`), with `_panel_resolve_role` defined at `:1358` (→ `canonical_staff_access.panel_role`). `:4865` is `applogin_poll_handler` and has nothing to do with this pair. The merge-target caution is correct and confirmed: `panel#clients` (maya-os-site/index.html:31305) is manager-scoped and renders `x.phone || x.email || 'Контакт скрыт'` for `d.customers`, while this handler returns names without phones, so folding them without carrying over BOTH the `is_master` gate and the phone suppression widens what a plain master sees — a 152-ФЗ-contour change, not a nav change. But correct the `staff_id` framing, which currently recommends the defect: `body.staff_id` is not a model of a safe server-validated scope parameter. api-proxy.php relays it verbatim from client input (fixture L867-877); the server accepts it on the `permissions.dashboard` bit alone and only `int()`-casts it — it is never checked against the salon roster — before `_master_clients_month(staff_id)` returns that master's client names plus `gross`/`personal`/`percent`. Neither live caller sends it, so it is an unexercised back door, not a precedent to preserve. And the widget contract sets the bar higher than "server-validated": FR-3's `assertNoCallerAuthority` forbids caller-supplied authority outright and `authority_hint` is read by no server decision, so the successor's scope must be DERIVED from the resolved role, with any client-supplied scope treated as a hint no decision reads. One small asymmetry in favour of the merge: retiring the mayaos.ru copy removes one of ~30 hardcoded cross-origin calls from the multi-tenant bundle into the single-tenant malesthetic proxy — marginal, not enough to call the pair an improvement. No frozen limitation is contradicted (nothing here touches attendance confirmation, STEP_UP, Gate 10, or approval role-gating).
